claims.text: The systematic review evaluated 40 articles on LLM applications in mental health published between January 2017 and April 2024.
15 evaluated articles (38%) focused on mental health conditions and suicidal ideation detection through text analysis.
7 evaluated articles (18%) focused on the use of LLMs as mental health conversational agents.
18 evaluated articles (45%) focused on other applications and evaluations of LLMs in mental health.
Clinical use of LLMs in mental health presents risks of inconsistencies in generated text.
Clinical use of LLMs in mental health presents risks of hallucination production.
Clinical use of LLMs in mental health lacks a comprehensive, benchmarked ethical framework.

evidence.description: In total, 40 articles were evaluated, published between January 1, 2017, and April 30, 2024.
including 15 (38%) articles on mental health conditions and suicidal ideation detection through text analysis
7 (18%) on the use of LLMs as mental health conversational agents
18 (45%) on other applications and evaluations of LLMs in mental health
These risks include inconsistencies in generated text
and the absence of a comprehensive, benchmarked ethical framework

methodologies.name: PRISMA Systematic Review
methodologies.description: A systematic review adhering to PRISMA guidelines searching 5 databases for publications on LLMs in mental health between 2017 and 2024.
conditions: Articles published between January 1, 2017, and April 30, 2024

limitations.text: The study excluded articles published in languages other than English.
Lack of multilingual datasets annotated by experts.
Challenges in interpretability due to the 'black box' nature of LLMs.

future_work.text: Continued research and development regarding LLMs as valuable clinical aids in mental health.
